page_2.details:
Silhouette: Fitted body-skimming bodice transitioning into a flared maxi skirt with asymmetric handkerchief hem
Sleeves: Full-length fitted set-in sleeves with no visible cuff opening
Other Features:
High close-fitting turtleneck collar approximately 2-3cm in height
Thigh-high slit on the front left skirt panel
Horizontal ruched gathering at the left hip transitioning to back waist

size_label.placement: Below or beside the brand label

care_label.placement: Inner left side seam, above 10–15 cm from the hem

page_3.label_notes: The color of the labels is white. Type of: 100% Recycled polyester woven label.

accessories.placement: Slit base at mid-thigh on left front skirt panel — applied before panel joining sequence
accessories.justification: Non-negotiable reinforcement at highest mechanical stress point in garment. Slit base concentrates all lateral leg movement force at a single termination point on matte jersey. Must be applied before skirt panel joining. Failure to reinforce is a primary QC failure point at QC High standard.
accessories.description: Bar-tack reinforcement — slit base - 100% Polyester core-spun thread, high-tenacity - 8–10 mm width
accessories.position: Slit base at mid-thigh on left front skirt panel — applied before panel joining sequence

accessories.item_description: Bar-tack reinforcement — ruched hip panel terminations
accessories.quantity: 2 per garment (one at each end of panel)
accessories.placement: Both termination ends of ruched hip panel on left skirt body
accessories.justification: Prevents horizontal ruching folds from migrating away from designed position under wear. Non-negotiable at a primary visible design feature at QC High standard.
accessories.description: Bar-tack reinforcement — ruched hip panel terminations - 100% Polyester core-spun thread - 8–10 mm width
accessories.qty: 2 per garment (one at each end of panel)
accessories.position: Both termination ends of ruched hip panel on left skirt body

accessories.item_description: Non-stretch stay tape — waist seam stabilization
accessories.dimensions: 4–6 mm width — applied along waist seam allowance before panel joining
accessories.placement: Interior waist seam allowance — inserted before lockstitch pass at waist panel join (SEAM 07)
accessories.justification: Maxi skirt weight on stretch jersey waist seam has documented risk of tunneling and waist seam position migration over wear cycles. Stabilization tape assessment required. Decision deferred to factory QC team in consultation with brand technical team. Must be confirmed before pre-production sample.
accessories.description: Non-stretch stay tape — waist seam stabilization - Woven polyester non-stretch stay tape - 4–6 mm width — applied along waist seam allowance before panel joining
accessories.position: Interior waist seam allowance — inserted before lockstitch pass at waist panel join (SEAM 07)

accessories.item_description: Hem point shaping template (cardboard or metal)
accessories.quantity: 1 set per hem point geometry — factory to produce from approved pattern
accessories.dimensions: Per pattern geometry for each angular hem point
accessories.placement: Used during hem finishing process — each angular hem point pressed to template before coverstitch application
accessories.justification: Asymmetric multi-point handkerchief hem requires each angular point individually shaped to exact geometry. Template ensures no two points vary in drop geometry. Required tooling at QC High standard for this construction complexity.
accessories.description: Hem point shaping template (cardboard or metal) - Cardboard or thin metal plate - Per pattern geometry for each angular hem point
accessories.qty: 1 set per hem point geometry — factory to produce from approved pattern
accessories.position: Used during hem finishing process — each angular hem point pressed to template before coverstitch application

seams.description: Structural join connecting front and back bodice panels at shoulder line, supporting sleeve cap weight.
seams.justification: Medium stress zone bearing sleeve weight. Enclosed overlock prevents viscose knit edge curl. Lockstitch primary ensures structural integrity; overlock secures cut edge. Allowances overlocked together and pressed toward back.

seams.description: Stretch-critical circumference seam running from armhole through fitted torso to skirt hem, carrying full body circumference stress.
seams.justification: No closure — side seams must accommodate full torso flex. 4-thread overlock ensures seam extends under stretch without thread failure. 12 mm allowance provides stability and allows pressing without tunneling. No topstitch — risk of puckering on matte jersey.

seams.description: Vertical structural seam running from waist panel join through full skirt length to multi-point handkerchief hem; must be perfectly straight and geometrically consistent.
seams.justification: High-visibility seam terminating into asymmetric hem geometry. Lockstitch ensures controlled straight seam path. Allowances pressed open (not together) to reduce bulk at hem point terminations and prevent visible ridging. Each allowance overlocked separately to prevent curl.

seams.description: Stretch-critical circumference seam joining turtleneck roll collar to bodice neckline; primary garment entry point with no closure.
seams.stitch_type: 4-Thread Overlock (504) primary + Coverstitch (406) topstitch to secure allowance
seams.justification: Sole garment entry mechanism — must sustain repeated stretch to full head circumference and recover without distortion. 4-thread overlock only appropriate primary stitch; lockstitch would break under head-entry stretch. High-tenacity thread prevents failure at repeated stretch cycles. Coverstitch topstitch lays internal allowance flat and prevents neck skin irritation.

seams.description: Reinforced load-bearing junction attaching full sleeve cap into bodice armhole; must flex with arm movement without distorting bodice silhouette.
seams.justification: High-stress junction combining sleeve weight bearing, lateral arm movement, and circumferential stretch simultaneously. Double-stitched construction is required to prevent seam failure under dynamic wear. Allowances enclosed together and turned into sleeve to reduce shoulder silhouette bulk.

seams.description: Full-length structural seam running from underarm to wrist along sleeve underside; must elongate with arm extension without rippling on matte jersey.
seams.justification: Full sleeve cap to wrist with no cuff break — seam must accommodate full elbow flex across full seam length. 4-thread overlock for stretch compatibility; lockstitch would cause thread pop at elbow flex. No topstitch — visible topstitch on matte jersey fitted upper arm inconsistent with clean minimalist design.

seams.description: Load-bearing horizontal panel join separating fitted bodice from flared skirt; must carry full maxi skirt weight without tunneling or rolling under tension.
seams.stitch_type: Lockstitch (301) + 4-Thread Overlock (504) + Coverstitch topstitch (406) at 2 mm from seam line; stabilization tape assessment required
seams.machine_type: Single Needle Lockstitch Machine + 4-Thread Overlock + Coverstitch Machine
seams.justification: Sole structural panel join bearing full maxi skirt weight plus ruched hip panel lateral stress. Unstabilized stretch jersey waist seam will tunnel and migrate under skirt weight. Lockstitch controls seam line position; overlock encloses edges; topstitch anchors allowances upward. 12 mm allowance accommodates stabilization tape if approved. Narrow non-stretch stay tape (4–6 mm) must be assessed before pre-production sample.
seams.machine: Single Needle Lockstitch Machine + 4-Thread Overlock + Coverstitch Machine

seams.description: Structural and aesthetic join securing the horizontally gathered ruched panel to the skirt body at left hip zone; must anchor gathering evenly and prevent fold migration.
seams.justification: Primary visible design element — ruching consistency must be validated panel-by-panel. Pre-ruching basting before final attachment prevents gathering shifting during lockstitch pass. Bar-tacking at panel ends is non-negotiable to prevent fold migration. Allowances enclosed and turned inward.

seams.description: Clean finished visible raw edge from slit base at mid-thigh to hem junction on left front skirt panel; slit base must be bar-tacked to prevent tearing under leg movement.
seams.stitch_type: Coverstitch (406) — stretch-compatible clean turned hem finish; bar-tack at slit base
seams.justification: Slit base is highest stress failure point — concentrates all lateral leg movement force at a single point. Bar-tack at slit base is non-negotiable and must be applied before panel joining sequence. Coverstitch provides stretch-compatible finish that will not crack or curl on exposed edge. Raw overlock at this visible location is not acceptable at QC High standard.

seams.description: Precision stretch-compatible narrow turned hem finish applied individually to each angular pointed hem panel; each point must be independently shaped, pressed, and finished.
seams.justification: Primary silhouette-defining design feature. Each angular point must be cut to exact geometry, individually pressed using a template, and stitched without altering geometry. Coverstitch maintains fabric mobility under drape — lockstitch would create rigid hem line restricting fabric swing and causing visible puckering. No two points may vary in drop geometry; feed tension must remain consistent across all panels.

seams.description: Clean turned standalone hem finish at wrist edge; no cuff opening or closure; must lie flat without raw curl on viscose knit.
seams.justification: No cuff or wrist closure — sleeve terminates at clean wrist hem. Coverstitch required over lockstitch as wrist hem must expand to allow hand passage; rigid lockstitch would restrict entry and crack under stretch. Viscose knit will curl aggressively at raw wrist edge — turned and coverstitch-secured finish is minimum acceptable.

measurements.description: Half-body circumference across fullest part of chest, controlling semi-fitted bodice width.
measurements.justification: Primary structural circumference controlling semi-fitted bodice width. Half-measurement per US women standard. Critical priority — deviation corrupts bodice fit across all panel seams.

measurements.description: Half-body circumference at natural waist, controlling fitted waist seam position.
measurements.justification: Controls waist seam fit in semi-fitted silhouette. Tight tolerance ± 0.64 cm reflects waist seam visibility and structural role as panel join. Critical priority.

measurements.description: Half-body circumference at fullest hip, controlling skirt ease and ruched panel placement zone.
measurements.justification: Controls hip ease through skirt zone and confirms ruched panel spatial context. Wider tolerance ± 1.27 cm reflects inherent fabric stretch at hip circumference. Critical priority.

measurements.description: Full width measured from shoulder point to shoulder point across back.
measurements.justification: Controls bodice shoulder width and sleeve cap seam placement. Tight tolerance reflects structural impact on armhole geometry. Critical priority.

measurements.point_of_measurement: HPS to Hem — Front (Shortest Hem Point)
measurements.description: Full length from high point shoulder to shortest front handkerchief hem point.
measurements.justification: Defines minimum hem drop of asymmetric silhouette. Must be measured and signed off individually per hem point. Tight tolerance non-negotiable — hem point geometry is primary design expression. Critical priority.

measurements.point_of_measurement: HPS to Hem — Back (Longest Trailing Point)
measurements.description: Full length from high point shoulder to longest trailing back handkerchief hem point.
measurements.justification: Defines maximum hem drop — 25 cm differential from front shortest point creates the asymmetric silhouette geometry. Must be individually measured against template. Any deviation corrupts asymmetric effect. Critical priority.

measurements.point_of_measurement: HPS to Hem — Mid Hem Point(s)
measurements.description: Full length from high point shoulder to intermediate handkerchief hem points between front and back extremes.
measurements.justification: Controls hem point graduation between shortest and longest points. Derived from similar asymmetric style. Important priority — mid-points define the visual transition of the handkerchief hem silhouette.

measurements.description: Full length from high point shoulder to waist panel seam on front bodice.
measurements.justification: Controls bodice length and waist seam vertical placement. Critical to ruched hip panel vertical positioning. Tight tolerance reflects structural dependency of waist seam on bodice-to-skirt join.

measurements.point_of_measurement: Sleeve Length (Shoulder Seam to Wrist Hem)
measurements.description: Full length from shoulder seam to wrist hem edge along sleeve underarm.
measurements.justification: Full long sleeve with no cuff break — sleeve length directly controls wrist coverage. Tightest tolerance in spec (± 0.27 cm) reflects visual sensitivity of wrist hem placement on fitted sleeve. Critical priority.

measurements.description: Half-body circumference at fullest bicep on set-in sleeve.
measurements.justification: Controls sleeve ease at upper arm for set-in sleeve construction. Wider tolerance ± 1.27 cm reflects stretch jersey accommodation. Important priority.

measurements.description: Half-body circumference at wrist hem opening.
measurements.justification: Controls wrist fit. Must be sufficient for hand passage without closure — minimum wrist opening on stretch jersey must accommodate hand entry. Important priority.

measurements.description: Full circumference of armhole measured on finished garment.
measurements.justification: Controls sleeve cap ease and armhole seam integrity. Full circumference measurement. Tight tolerance reflects structural load at armhole junction. Critical priority.

measurements.description: Full height of turtleneck collar from neckline join to folded top edge.
measurements.justification: Controls turtleneck roll height. Not graded as collar height is a fixed design proportion independent of size grading. Tolerance ± 0.5 cm reflects visual sensitivity at face level. Critical priority.

measurements.description: Half-body circumference of neck opening at turtleneck base join.
measurements.justification: Controls garment entry — must stretch to accommodate full head circumference (approx 56–58 cm) without closure. Half-measurement of 19 cm yields 38 cm relaxed — stretch jersey must achieve head entry. Critical priority.

measurements.description: Full length of front slit from slit base to hem junction on left panel.
measurements.justification: Controls leg opening depth at front slit. Not graded — slit length is a fixed design proportion. Derived from similar style. Tight tolerance ± 0.64 cm as slit length affects modesty and silhouette. Critical priority.

measurements.description: Full width of ruched hip panel measured after ruching is applied.
measurements.justification: Controls finished panel width post-ruching. Not graded — panel is a fixed design feature at left hip. Wider tolerance ± 1.27 cm reflects inherent variation in gathered fabric. Pre- and post-ruching width must be documented by pattern maker. Important priority.

measurements.point_of_measurement: Ruched Hip Panel Vertical Placement (from waist seam)
measurements.description: Full vertical distance from waist seam to top edge of ruched hip panel.
measurements.justification: Controls vertical placement of ruched panel on skirt body. Graded to maintain consistent hip zone proportion across sizes. Tight tolerance preserves designed panel placement relative to waist seam. Important priority.

measurements.description: Half-body circumference of hem sweep across all panels — reference measurement only.
measurements.justification: Reference measurement capturing total hem width across asymmetric multi-point panels. Used for cut planning and fabric consumption reference. Wider tolerance ± 1.5 cm reflects inherent variability of asymmetric hem geometry. Reference priority only — not a pass/fail QC point.

fabrics.description: Shell Fabric — 90% Viscose / 10% Elastane, Stretch Jersey Knit, 200–240 GSM, 2-Way Stretch, Matte Surface, Jet Black
fabrics.position: Entire outer shell — turtleneck collar, bodice, sleeves, ruched hip panel, skirt, all handkerchief hem points
fabrics.justification: Viscose base provides superior drape fluidity for ruched hip panel and multi-point handkerchief hem. Elastane at 8–10% enables stretch entry at turtleneck with no closure while maintaining semi-fitted bodice structure. 200–240 GSM targets Fall 25 weight while permitting hem swing. Matte finish consistent with jet black Fall positioning. High opacity is non-negotiable given absence of lining.

quality_standards.comments: 90% viscose is highly prone to shrinkage and lengthwise distortion after washing. Critical for this garment: any shrinkage will corrupt asymmetric handkerchief hem point geometry and slit placement, both of which are irreversible on cut panels.

Jet black is a high-dye-load colorway requiring confirmation that color is retained after laundering without bleed or fading. Viscose fibers can release dye under wash agitation and elevated temperature.

Jet black on viscose jersey is high-risk for wet crocking onto skin and light undergarments. Direct skin contact along side seams, inner arm, and turtleneck collar zone increases transfer risk. Wet rubbing requirement reflects perspiration exposure in close-fitting bodice.
Jet black colorway on a viscose base is susceptible to surface dulling and undertone shift under UV exposure. Daily womenswear end use with outdoor exposure warrants light fastness verification.

Multiple high-stress seams confirmed: side seams bearing full torso circumference load, armhole seam supporting sleeve weight, waist panel join carrying full maxi skirt weight, and slit base absorbing lateral leg movement. Failure at any of these points is a critical QC fault on this construction.

Ruched hip panel gathering must retain structured fold formation after washing. Turtleneck roll must return to correct height and lay flat. Asymmetric hem points must not distort. Viscose jersey is prone to surface disturbance and seam puckering after agitation.

Stretch jersey knit surface is susceptible to pilling under friction, particularly at high-contact zones: underarm, inner sleeve, and turtleneck collar. Matte finish amplifies pill visibility. Viscose fiber loops in knit structure are more prone to entanglement than filament synthetics.

10% elastane content supports stretch entry at turtleneck as the sole garment entry point. If recovery is insufficient, the neckline will permanently deform after head entry, collapsing roll height and distorting the close-fitting bodice silhouette. Critical functional test for this garment.

Stretch jersey knit construction requires bursting strength rather than tensile tear testing. Relevant across all omnidirectional stress zones: armhole, side seam, and slit base under dynamic movement. Ensures knit structure does not rupture under peak load during normal wear.

Stretch jersey knits are prone to fabric spirality caused by knit loop imbalance. On a maxi-length dress with a center back seam and asymmetric hem, any post-wash torque will rotate seams off-grain, shift the front slit laterally, and misalign handkerchief hem points. Must be confirmed before bulk cut approval.

size_chart.pom: E - HPS to Hem Front / Shortest Hem Point (cm)
F - HPS to Hem Back / Longest Hem Point (cm)
G - HPS to Hem Mid Point (cm)
H - HPS to Waist Seam Front (cm)
P - Ruched Hip Panel Width (cm) [Not Graded]
Q - Ruched Hip Panel Vertical Placement from Waist Seam (cm)

wash_label.washing_instructions: Hand wash cold or machine wash gentle cycle, cold water (30°C max). Wash inside out. Do not wring.
wash_label.drying_instructions: Do not tumble dry. Lay flat to dry away from direct heat and sunlight.
wash_label.ironing_instructions: Cool iron only (110°C max). Iron inside out. Do not iron on ruched panel or handkerchief hem points directly — use pressing cloth.

dry_cleaning.line_1: Dry clean permitted — solvent F only.
dry_cleaning.line_2: Professional dry clean recommended for optimal garment longevity.

standards: ISO 3758 care labelling symbols required for US market export
ASTM D5489 US care label symbol standard
FTC Care Labeling Rule (16 CFR Part 423) — US market mandatory
Country of origin statement required on care label
Fiber content statement required per FTC Textile Fiber Products Identification Act
wash_label.justification: Viscose/elastane stretch jersey requires cold gentle wash to prevent dimensional distortion and fiber damage. Viscose is prone to shrinkage and loss of dimensional stability under heat and mechanical agitation — gentle/hand wash cold is the safest instruction preserving garment geometry including ruched panel and handkerchief hem points. No bleach — jet black dye lot vulnerable to bleach degradation. No tumble dry — heat and mechanical action will distort elastane recovery and cause shrinkage in viscose. Lay flat drying preserves semi-fitted silhouette geometry. Cool iron only — viscose scorches at high heat; matte surface must not be glazed by iron contact. Dry clean permitted as secondary care option. US market regulatory compliance requires FTC care label rule, fiber content, and country of origin.

care_label_instructions: The care label must contain carelabel symbols and those only.
Care label must be made in recycled polyester.
Care labels must contain origin: made in India.
Care labels must be given the same size, font and style.
